# Fixed: Link extra files imported with a track to its track file

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. It is stacked on [`fix/replace-import-rollback`](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/fix/replace-import-rollback), which reworks the same import loop, and merges after it.

With Import Extra Files on, a download's lyrics (`.lrc`, `.txt`) and other extra files are imported beside each track. Develop imports them inside the track loop of `ImportApprovedTracks`, before `AddMany` saves the new track files, so each track file still has id 0 and every extra file row is stored with `TrackFileId` 0. Renaming the tracks then leaves those extra files behind under the old names, and deleting or upgrading the track leaves them in the album folder. The artist scan keeps such a row as long as its file is on disk.

- Extra files are imported after `AddMany` (and after each album's backed-up files are settled), so each row links to its track file. An extra file that fails to import logs a warning; the track still counts as imported. Before, the failure marked the already-moved track "Failed to import track".
- Two housekeeping tasks, ported from Sonarr's `CleanupOrphanedExtraFiles` and `CleanupOrphanedSubtitleFiles`, delete `ExtraFiles` and `LyricFiles` rows whose artist or track file is gone, as `CleanupOrphanedMetadataFiles` does for `MetadataFiles`. A row stored with `TrackFileId` 0 is linked to the track file in its folder whose name, followed by a dot, starts the file's name (the longest such name, so `Mr. Blue Sky.lrc` goes to `Mr. Blue Sky.flac`, not `Mr.flac`): an extra file is named after its track file when it's imported. A row that no track file matches, because its track was renamed since, keeps `TrackFileId` 0 as before. Sonarr deletes such rows; here the artist scan would then pick a file up again only if it could parse the name to a track.

Linking every imported extra file makes the code that removes a track file's extras reach all of them, where before it reached only those the artist scan had linked. Three of its callers removed extras they shouldn't, and one that should didn't:
- Removing a root folder in settings drops only Lidarr's rows now, as a cleanup with no history entry. Before, it counted as deleting each track file, so the extras beside the files went to the recycle bin (or were deleted, with no recycle bin set) while the audio stayed.
- A file imported again at the same path (a rescan after a tagger changed it, or after a release switch unlinked its tracks) keeps its extras: their rows move to the file's new row once it's saved. Before, they were recycled.
- Deleting an album with its files recycles its extra files too, lyrics and metadata files included. Before, they stayed behind and kept the album folder from being removed as empty.

Tests: extra files imported with a track over the real services and test database (both rows linked to the new track file; failed before the change with `TrackFileId` 0); an extra file import that throws (the track still imports, with a warning); each housekeeping rule for both tables, including a row that must stay; relinking by name (the dot after the track's name, the longest name, the album, and a row nothing matches). Through the real media file, deletion and extra file services: a removed root folder keeps the extras on disk; a user's track file deletion recycles them; an album deleted with its files recycles them, and one deleted without keeps them; a file imported again, changed or after a release switch, keeps its extras linked to its new row; the container resolves all three extra file services as relinkers. Each was broken on purpose and caught by a test.
